[Rating: 1/10] Dumb and pointless;  neither a fun game nor a wargame.  I thought my kids would learn a bit of history, and instead they called it "unrealistic"!  Commands & Colors: Ancients is far superior.  Or, put it this way:  M'44 is right up there with Mickey Mouse Yahtzee, which really doesn't give the latter it's due credit...  I wrote those words at least two years ago, and I stand by them. [Rating: 1/10] This game is the McDonalds of wargames. It sucks balls if you had a real hamburger but most people have incredibly banal taste...

[Rating: 1/10] What I really hate: There are a lot of games like Memoir '44. It is not new nor has it new ideas. Therefore the note might not be the "real" one, but I'm totally fed up with always the same stuff

[Rating: 1/10] I bought Command & Colors: Ancients for my son when he was 4, but I was a bit disappointed. Unfortunately, my mother-in-law bought this game for him and it's even worse. CC: Ancients is boring and tedious, but at least it's a game, in the sense that you have to consider several tactical options, including defending, and the flow of the game is more or less like a real battle. Memoir 44 is not a game at all, and bears no resemblance to anything. It's actually a toy, not a game.

[Rating: 1/10] The single worst war game ever made.  Pure luck.  No strategy.  I don't care how much strategy you think you have, all the luck in this game will take it away.  If you are looking for a 100% war luck strategy(uh, scratch that last word) game, this is it.  You will see one troop take out 15 tanks and 15 troops with no return fire.  Yes, only THIS game can do that.  You could be down to your last troop and win this game.  You will NEVER find a game with this much luck. [Rating: 1/10] Terrible, terrible game.  The combat system doesn't roll enough dice, which makes it too swingy; all the tactics in the world won't save you if your opponent rolls 8/8 hits.

[Rating: 1/10] It had been so long since my last play I forgot why I disliked this so much.  Luck of the dice is fine. Luck of the draw is fine.  Both luck of the draw and luck of the dice together? Makes for a very one sided experience if you are the one who gets unlucky.  Drawing random cards to be able to move means you can be unlucky and be unable to move the troops you need/want to move. In this last game I kept drawing activate right flank cards while having very little on my right flank. All four of my cards remained that way for most of the game.
